model.rationale: The district's ten-point Democratic lean, Peters's incumbency, and a lopsided financial gap — $2.6 million on hand against about $4,000 raised for Cohen — all point to an easy hold, and markets price a Peters win near 96 percent.
model.watch: Late outside spending for Cohen or unusually low, uneven turnout in the top-two general could narrow the margin, though no such signs are visible yet.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by ten points. He has raised more than $2.1 million and holds $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Steve Cohen has reported about $4,000 in receipts and drawn no outside support. Prediction markets price a Peters win at roughly 96 percent, and no public polling or expert ratings suggest the race is competitive.

The absence of polling is the main source of uncertainty, but the fundamentals all point the same way: the district's partisan lean, Peters's incumbency advantage, and an overwhelming resource gap. A low-turnout general could compress the margin somewhat, yet nothing in the available evidence indicates Cohen has the funding or profile to close a deficit of this size. The seat remains safely in Democratic hands barring an unforeseen shift.
